name: Consumed by Greed
oracle_text:
Gift a card (You may promise an opponent a gift as you cast this spell. If you do, they draw a card before its other effects.)
Target opponent sacrifices a creature with the greatest power among creatures they control. If the gift was promised, return target creature card from your graveyard to your hand.
blocked_sentences: Target opponent sacrifices a creature with the greatest power among creatures they control. If the gift was promised, return target creature card from your graveyard to your hand.

needs.what: a target spec that is declared only when the gift was promised -- e.g. a `count_if_gift` (or a general `variant: "gift_promised"`) on a TargetModel/TargetSpec, parallel to `count_if_kicked`, so "return target creature card from your graveyard to your hand" is a second target {kind: card, selector: {zone: graveyard, owner: you, types: [Creature]}} with count 0 on the unpromised cast and 1 on each promised cast, with target enumeration in the cast-options code building a separate tuple set for the gift variants
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The casting code computes the target tuples once and hands the identical list to the unpromised `_cast_variant` and to every gift-promisee variant, so the promise cannot change what the spell points at. `count_if_kicked` is the existing per-variant target count, but the loader accepts it only on a card with `kicker`/`multikicker`, and a gift is not a kicker (the loader refuses a free kicker). Declaring the graveyard target unconditionally and gating the return with `if {gift_promised: true}` is not the card: an unpromised cast would then require a creature card in your graveyard to be castable at all, and would announce a target the printed spell never chooses. `optional: true` makes the second target the caster's free choice rather than the promise's consequence (a promised cast could skip it). `mode` gates a spec on a cast-time choice but only on a single top-level `choose_mode`. Everything else on the card is expressible: `gift: "a card"` with `{op: draw, player: gift_recipient}` (as parting_gust/perch_protection write their gifts), a target-player spec, and `sacrifice` with `objects: {controller: {target: t1}, types: [Creature], zone: battlefield, count: 1, chooser: owner, extreme: {of: power, pick: greatest}}`; only the gift-gated target blocks it. Same need as into_the_flood_maw.
